steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and stir, constantly, until the mixture becomes paste-like, about 3 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk, and bring to a simmer, stirring constantly. Reduce heat to medium-low, and cook, stirring occasionally, until thickened, 5 to 10 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper.
Separate the hard-cooked egg whites from the yolks. Roughly chop whites and stir into sauce. Press egg yolks through a mesh strainer and set aside.
Place a slice of toast on a plate; ladle 1/2 cup sauce over top. Garnish with egg yolks and a sprinkle of paprika.

raw_recipe.headline: Goldenrod Eggs
raw_recipe.description: Goldenrod eggs combine hard-cooked eggs in a creamy white béchamel sauce served over slices of toast for a delicious family breakfast tradition.

video.description: This method of cooking eggs will take your breakfast game to an entirely new level. In this video, Nicole shows you how to make Goldenrod Eggs with a smooth and delicious egg gravy. After hard boiling the eggs, separate the yolks from the egg whites. Chop the egg whites and add them into a cream and flour mixture over the stove to make the gravy. Next, pour the gravy over a plate of toast before grating the yolk over the top for the goldenrod-esque color.

review.reviewBody: My oldest who thinks everything is disgusting had 2 helpings, so I guess it was a success. I did the recipe from nothing prepared. Cooked the bacon, gathered the eggs, hard boiled the eggs, peeled the eggs, picked the onions from the yard, wash and chop. A little time consuming when the piranhas are circling. I added baby porter bella mushrooms because why not. I have to use the slap chop to mince them and then hide them so the kids dont see. I sauteed them in some of the bacon grease and added it to the egg white filling. Haha they didn't notice. I used the slap chop on the egg whites and bacon as well. highly recommend the slap chop, it's a time saver. It did have a nice presentation when served. The only thing I didn't have was chipotle Tabasco sauce. Ultimately, if the kids like it, I'll do it again with a little prep work from the day before.

I make this quite often. Here are some possible improvements - cut the toast up into bite size pieces, sprinkle chopped bacon over the toast - then cover with the white sauce - serve on warm plates. I pre size the toast and bacon to enable the customer to not to waste time cutting it up - hence letting it cool. The warm plate helps also. I also double if not triple up on the egg yolk topping - sprinkle paprika on the top if you so desire.

I grew up eating Eggs Goldenrod (yes, that's what we called it). I'm turning 50 this year and this has ALWAYS been my #1 favorite meal of all time. This recipe is exactly the same as what my parents have always made me, even now. My husband wanted to surprise me with this meal, so he's the one who found this particular recipe and made it because he didn't want to ruin the surprise by asking ME for my family recipe. Wow, it was amazing. And in his research, he found several people say it's great with nutmeg sprinkled over top. So we tried it and WOW, amazing. I like it the old fashioned way...just as is without bacon or onion. But the nutmeg really is amazing. And I absolutely prefer pushing the yolks through a sieve, creating a fine "snow" of yolk and not chunks of yolk. I like a thick white bread (even though I'm normally a health nut and normally eat whole grain...but there are times you just don't change a recipe). This is amazing.

I grew up eating this and have continued the tradition. We had it for any meal, not just breakfast. Only exception is instead of whole milk, we use 2 cans of evaporated milk and 1 1/2 cans of water, add water last but add it gradually. Make sure to stir constantly to prevent sticking. Also, we didn’t toast the bread.

My mother made this for us often for weekend breakfasts. She called it Eggs on a Goldenrod. I’ve never heard anyone else call it that. We are southern so she fried bacon and used the bacon grease to make gravy, scrambled the eggs then added them and the crumbled bacon to the gravy poured over toast. I still make it and now my daughter makes it. I’m sure the the bechamel sauce is good but I need the gravy for the great flavor.

My family has Golden Rod Eggs every Easter and tradition from my Grandmother. We separate the cooked whites from the yolk and crumple the yolk up with salt, pepper and paprika. Whites go into the white sauce and yolk sprinkled on top. We invite family, friends and neighbors for it and served on toast. Asparagus, strawberries, and ham round out the breakfast. My Grandmother was from between Germany and France her last name was Noh. It is a feast!

I love this. We make it yearly Easter morning to use up Easter eggs. A pinch of nutmeg and couple tablespoons dry sherry elevates it. One of the best ways to eat hard boiled eggs. The paprika is a nice touch.

The answer for what to do with all of those Easter Eggs is--Goldenrod Toast. My mother fixed this every Easter. Most of my sister's and brother make this also. I like many tweak it a bit. A few drops of Tabasco, a dash of garlic powder, and more white pepper than you think. I like the Dijon mustard idea. In fact, my wife requested Goldenrod Toast for breakfast tomorrow morning; so she will get the mustard addition. It's not just for Easter.

My father made this for us when we were young, very southern dish that fed 6 growing kids. Of course we tripled the ingredients. As an adult, I serve this but changed up some of the ingredients to add some flavor. Instead of white bread we use sour dough or whole grain. I also add 1/2 cup of grated parmesan which gives it a little kick.
I love the concept, because my husband loves breakfast gravy, and these are ingredients we always have on hand. It needed a little more flavor to me, and adding some dijon mustard did the trick.

This is what we grew up eating! 6 kids, mom called it creamed eggs on toast. Simply slice boiled eggs on toasted bread with white cream gravy on top. A quick, easy and filling breakfast for our large family.

Very easy to make my mother-in-law makes the same thing sometimes I mix some of the yolk with the eggs never had it with paprika. That was really good to give it a kick and more flavor. Thanks for the suggestion loved it.

My grandmother use to make this when I was a kid(73 now) when the chickens laid too many eggs. She served over buttered toast. So yummy. Today, I'll make a small batch (I put the yokes in the sauce) and eat it like a soup to cut down on the calories of the bread. comfort food at it's best.
I have enjoyed this breakfast for years. It is in my 80 year old Settlement cookbook. It is a smaller portion in the book. Listed as Goldenrod Toast.

I learned to make this in Jr. High Home Economics class. I am now 77 years old and still love it. It is exactly what I learned to make back them and it was called the same thing. It seems special recipes always last!
One thing my mom cooked every holiday for breakfast. I’ve added a pinch of nutmeg, or added crumbled bacon or sausage as an adult. But just the way the recipe is printed is just right as well.
My Gramma used to make these. This recipe is so good!
